newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai, Daewoo to buy Kia Steel stakes.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai, Daewoo to buy Kia Steel stakes.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co and Daewoo Motor Co have agreed in principle to buy stakes in Kia Steel Co, a Kia Group statement said on Thursday.
The agreement was reached in a meeting on Thursday by Hyundai Motor honorary chairman Chung Se-yung, Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong and Kia Group chairman Kim Sun-hong, the statement said.
Kia officials said the move was aimed at saving Kia Steel, one of core units of the Kia Group which has run into financial troubles.
Under the agreement, Hyundai Motor, Daewoo Motor and Kia Motors Corp would form a consortium to run Kia Steel, it said. The three carmakers will have equal stakes in Kia Steel.
The statement said the three automakers agreed to start working-level negotiations to work out details of the consortium.
Kia Group's creditors have selected 18 of the group's 38 affiliates for bail-out under a scheme they forged voluntarily in April to prevent major companies from folding.
A meeting on Wednesday of Kia creditors failed to produce results as creditors ruled that the group's self-rescue plans were not sufficient.
